reviews.title: 8 Years

Mediation on its own I do not think would have been as life changing. I just sat my first retreat a couple of months ago and had a tremendous shift in my perception. I think the app laid a great foundation of theory and practice that allowed me to release, open, and view life another way.

reviews.title: Apple Watch app requested.
reviews.text:
The content in Waking Up is excellent, but the app could be much better integrated into the Apple ecosystem.

An Apple Watch app would be incredibly useful — especially the ability to download and listen to meditations and other content directly from the Watch with AirPods, without needing an iPhone nearby.

I’d also love to see better native AirPlay integration. The current custom audio player can be a little buggy with my HomePod setup, particularly when switching speakers or controlling playback.

The content is already great. Better Apple Watch, AirPlay, and HomePod support would make the actual listening experience significantly better.

reviews.title: Course ends after 30 days
reviews.text:
I subscribed to this app based on the introductory course that builds each lesson on the previous lessons. $150 for a year of what I thought was going to be lessons that would take me deeper into my meditation practice. 30 days later, after they have your money they cleverly change the format to a generic daily 10 minute meditation. There are free apps that offer the same thing. 

They also claim they will refund your money if you email support. I did so on July 19. It’s now July 30 and they are still “processing” the refund, which I’ve come to expect will not be sent. I’ll update this if they do refund my remaining 11 months but would never recommend this deceptive app to anyone.

Edit: Refund finally received on August 6

reviews.title: Sam is a Wonderful Guide
reviews.text: I’ve been a fairly close admirer of Sam’s work since I was in college studying the humanities. This app has been extremely helpful getting back into the practice of meditation. Sam is a master of language and uses guiding principles that universalize the wide variety of experiences one may have in this practice. I’ve listened to more religious or more mystical guides, and ironically enough I find myself—or lack thereof—more mystified by Sam’s approach. Also a lot of really great clips and pieces of wisdom that can keep you occupied and thinking constructively for hours. Can’t express my gratitude enough for this app!

reviews.title: Hold On
reviews.text:
I’ve been surprised by how impactful this app has been. It’s not so much the thoughtfulness of the app itself, and it is thoughtfully designed, it’s more the content and guidance of Sam’s voice that I’ve come to trust in some sense. Nearly everything these days has an agenda for me. Sometimes it’s subtle, but it’s usually recognizable if I listen to the sensations in my body. For me, Sam is one of a few people I can sit under and allow his voice to guide me deeper. And deeper this rabbit hole seems to go. I can sense an unraveling in my mind that’s both scary and thrilling because it feels like real change. It feels like freedom.

Thanks Sam & team.

reviews.title: Full of knowledge, wisdom, advise, humor from wonderful teachers
reviews.text:
I started this app after hearing Sam on Dan Harris’s app and was at first a little overwhelmed by so much content.  Began slowly, with the daily meditation and soon found myself on a whole new level of my practice.  Sam’s approach for me was unique  and introduced me quickly to the part of my mind that is separate from thoughts and sensations.  Here was a friendly, peaceful state that I could go to at any moment!
Soon I started the sleep talks and meditations which are now my nightly habits.  Once I began exploring Theory, Practice, Conversations I knew this app had it all and stopped using the other apps I had followed for years.
Thank you for this incredibly rich material.  You are truly doing a wonderful service to we seekers.

reviews.title: Mediation as it should be practiced
reviews.text: Having attempted meditation over the past few years, I had come to believe that mindfulness was primarily a focusing exercise. You learn to focus on breathing, to the exclusion of all else, and learn to apply this skill more generally. All the other impacts others described seemed down stream of this focus, and those that weren’t I believed to be made up. After giving this app a few months, I can say that I was completely incorrect. I won’t argue for it here, but meditation is the practice of “self”-knowledge (and for those who have worked through the courses I use the word self generously here). It is a genuinely profound experience to realize you have lived your entire being drowned in thought, and to finally hear that torrent of noise as it is. The meditation practices provided here do really give the sense of “waking up”, for the first time. I would recommend this practice to anyone, I think Harris and the other instructors on here do a very good job, and there are a wide variety of courses focusing on Cognitive behavioral therapy, more spiritual versions of meditation, self knowledge, gratitude, analyzing consciousness. Meditation is much more expansive than I thought it was. This may sound unrealistic to those who haven’t tried it (it certainly was to me). Just try going in with an open mind, I feel highly confident it will change how you see yourself and the world.
